summary: This article explains how penguins swim, stay warm, raise their chicks, find food, and hide from predators in icy Antarctica, and how melting sea ice affects them.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “Penguins of Antarctica” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: a thick layer of fat under the skin of some animals that helps keep them warm
to crowd very close together, often to stay warm or safe
very small sea animals that look like shrimp

challengeTerms.def: a material or layer that stops heat from escaping
to keep an egg warm so that it can develop and hatch
a machine that circles Earth in space and can take pictures or send signals

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that penguins are better suited to their home than almost any other animal? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how emperor penguin parents share the work of raising a chick.
struggling: Pre-teach blubber, huddle, and krill with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use insulation, incubate, and satellite in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
